newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes sharply lower in hectic trading.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes sharply lower in hectic trading.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed around its lows on Thursday after a busy day's trading, dealers said.

"It was a pretty hectic day. It has really dominated by stop-loss selling in kiwi-yen. Obviously with the (U.S.) dollar coming lower on the yen it has forced some of the longs on the kiwi-yen to sell out," a Wellington chief dealer said.
The kiwi closed at US$0.7064/71 after hitting a high of 0.7118 in morning trading.
On the Trade Weighted Index the kiwi closed down 57 basis points lower at 67.36.
"The local market was caught long at the end of the day and sold it really from 0.7095 straight back down to 0.7080," the chief dealer said.
"If the dollar-yen looks to be going lower they may hang off a little bit and we may see kiwi going a little lower."
He said political news had "added to the whole query".

Reports that Labour leader Helen Clark had mentioned the option of a vote of no confidence if a new government was not formed by negotiations before parliament was due to meet on December 13 had left the market uncertain.
"We are not quite sure what she was on about. The market has been too busy today to digest it to be honest," he said.

Labour and the conservative caretaker National government are negotiating over the shape of a new government with nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power after an election on October 12.
A report that Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen had again called the dollar too high brought the kiwi off a little too.
"It adds to the worry and once you see offshore selling, the market comes off pretty quickly and that's what we've seen today. They are still chasing yields," the chief dealer said.
He picked an overnight range of 0.7060 to 0.7100 for the kiwi.
